t: TPM 2.0: The Root of Trust in Every Machine
title: TPM 2.0: The Root of Trust in Every Machine
description: The Trusted Platform Module 2.0 is a tamper-resistant crypto-processor — usually a chip on the motherboard — specified by the Trusted Computing Group. It generates and stores cryptographic keys where software cannot reach them, measures boot software into Platform Configuration Registers, and anchors attestation. Most modern PCs and servers ship with one.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Platform Configuration Registers (PCRs)
description: PCRs are the TPM's measurement log: each boot component hashes the next and 'extends' the PCR (new = hash(old || measurement)), so any change anywhere in the boot chain changes the final values. 24 PCRs cover firmware, bootloader, kernel, and more. Sealed data only unseals when PCRs match the trusted state.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Measured Boot vs Secure Boot
description: Measured boot records what ran (into PCRs) without stopping anything; secure boot verifies signatures and refuses to run the untrusted. They compose: secure boot enforces policy, measured boot provides evidence. Attestation then reports the measurements to a verifier. Defense systems want all three.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: The Endorsement Key (EK) and Attestation
description: The Endorsement Key is the TPM's factory-installed identity — a certificate from the manufacturer vouches that this is a genuine TPM. Remote attestation quotes PCR values signed by an attestation key chained to the EK, proving to a remote verifier what software the machine booted. Zero-trust networks admit machines on attestation, not on claims.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Sealed Storage
description: Sealing encrypts data to a TPM key bound to PCR values: the data decrypts only on the same TPM with the same boot measurements. Disk encryption keys, VPN credentials, and license tokens get sealed so stolen drives stay dark on foreign machines. Change the bootloader and the seal will not open.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

t: TPM Key Hierarchy: EK, SRK, and Children
title: TPM Key Hierarchy: EK, SRK, and Children
description: TPM keys form a hierarchy: the Endorsement Key at the root, the Storage Root Key guarding stored keys, and child keys for signing, encryption, and attestation. Parent keys wrap children, so deleting a parent destroys the subtree — crypto-shredding by design. Hierarchies organize trust the way directories organize files.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Hardware Security Modules (HSMs)
description: HSMs are the datacenter-grade cousins of TPMs: rack or PCIe appliances (Thales Luna, YubiHSM, AWS CloudHSM) that generate, store, and use keys in certified tamper-resistant hardware. Certificate authorities, code signing, and payment keys live in HSMs. FIPS 140-3 Level 3/4 certifies the tamper resistance.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: FIPS 140-3: The Certification Bar
description: FIPS 140-3 (successor to 140-2) is the US/Canada standard certifying cryptographic modules: Level 1 is software-only, Level 2 adds tamper-evidence, Level 3 adds tamper-resistance and identity auth, Level 4 adds active tamper response. Defense procurement requires certified modules. The level must match the threat.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: TPM 2.0 Algorithms: The Crypto Menu
description: TPM 2.0 is algorithm-agile: RSA, ECC (NIST and BN curves), AES, SHA-256/SHA-384, HMAC, plus key derivation. Agility mattered because algorithms age — the TPM that could not learn new math would become a liability. Post-quantum algorithms are the next menu update the industry is preparing.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

t: BitLocker, LUKS, and TPM-Bound Disk Encryption
title: BitLocker, LUKS, and TPM-Bound Disk Encryption
description: OS disk encryption binds to the TPM: BitLocker seals keys to PCRs on Windows, LUKS can seal via Clevis on Linux. The drive decrypts transparently on the trusted machine and stays encrypted everywhere else. This is sealed storage at OS scale — the everyday face of the TPM.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Supply-Chain and Platform Attestation
description: Attestation scales from one machine to fleets: every node quotes its boot state, verifiers admit only known-good measurements, and unknown firmware never joins the cluster. Supply-chain attacks that modify firmware get caught at admission. The network's immune system is cryptographic.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: TPM Provisioning and Ownership
description: Taking TPM ownership sets the storage root and authorization values — the administrative act that binds the TPM to its owner. Clear ownership wipes the hierarchy (crypto-shredding everything). Provisioning is done once, carefully, and audited. Ownership is the root of the root of trust.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Common Criteria and EAL
description: Beyond FIPS, high-assurance HSMs pursue Common Criteria Evaluation Assurance Levels — EAL4+ for commercial defense use. EAL measures how thoroughly the security was evaluated, not just what it claims. Procurement stacks FIPS plus Common Criteria for the highest bars.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

t: The Full Trust Chain, Silicon to Service
title: The Full Trust Chain, Silicon to Service
description: Ladder-top trust: silicon identity (EK) measures firmware (PCRs), secure boot enforces, attestation proves to verifiers, sealed keys protect data, HSMs guard the crown jewels. Fifteen rungs from a chip to a network that only admits machines it can prove trustworthy.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Key Ceremonies
description: HSM master keys are born in key ceremonies: multiple custodians, audited scripts, video recording, split knowledge so no one person ever knows the whole key. The ceremony is the human half of hardware trust. Boring, meticulous, and absolutely essential.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.
